transcript:
Meeting header: Date: 2026-07-07 16:00 UTC; Duration: 46 minutes; Attendees: Evan Brooks (Redwood AE), Lina Cho (Redwood SE), Marcus Lee (AutumnBridge), Priya Nair (AutumnBridge), Olivia Chen (AutumnBridge - Security), Ethan Park (AutumnBridge - Infra)

Auto Summary: Quick discovery on p95 latency and streaming throughput. AutumnBridge is evaluating Redwood hosted for a pilot but has hard security and compliance gating that may push them to Dedicated or Private. Primary performance asks: sub-350ms p95 for simple responses, streaming support for up to ~7k tokens at 50-80 tok/sec, and burst concurrency up to ~200 streams with graceful fallbacks.

Topics: p95 targets, tokens/sec for streaming, KV/prefix cache behavior, burst concurrency sizing, routing/fallbacks, private deployment KMS and audit logs.

Action items (recapped): see metadata.

Transcript Body:
[00:00] Evan: Hey everyone, thanks for taking time today, I'm Evan from Redwood, i'll hand over to Lina our solutions engineer to do the deep part, but first quick intro?
[00:06] Marcus: Yep thanks, Marcus here, head of ML at AutumnBridge. We're evaluating infra for our new live-summarization product, lots of streaming responses and bursts during end-of-day reports.
[00:12] Priya: Hi, priya platform eng, we'll own integration.
[00:15] Olivia: Olivia, security lead, I have a list of compliance Qs.
[00:18] Lina: Great, quick agenda: confirm p95 targets, discuss streaming tokens/sec, concurrency/burst model, hosted vs dedicated vs private overhead, next steps.
[00:26] Evan: rough timebox 45 minutes, hop in.

[02:00] Lina: Marcus, what's the p95 target you're designing to today and what's the worst case you need to survive?
[02:07] Marcus: We're aiming for p95 under 350ms for short flavored replies like "summaries < 300 tokens". For longer streaming responses we want the first token under 250ms then streaming at 50-80 tokens/sec; overall tail shouldn't exceed maybe 1s per chunk but p95 cap is the priority. Also, daily peak bursts: about 150-200 concurrent active streams for 10-20 minutes.
[02:33] Lina: ok and what's your model footprint? are you using an open LLM or closed models?
[02:37] Marcus: We'll start with LlamaX-13B quantized but flexibility to test LlamaX-70B if quality requires; latency budget is tight so quantization and small optimal kernels matter.
[02:45] Lina: makes sense — on Redwood hosted we have tuned kernels and dynamic batching, we can route to smaller model variants as fallback. For dedicated you get reserved capacity so burst handling may be simpler but cost is higher.

[05:10] Priya: We're also worried about cold start for streaming endpoints, how long to spin up and what warm pool sizes do you recommend?
[05:17] Lina: warm pools depend on model size and expected concurrency, for 13B quantized i'd suggest a small steady pool and autoscale thresholds; coldstart for a new instance is around 4-7 seconds on GPU infra, but in practice continuous batching and cache warm-up make first streaming token fast if you reuse instances.
[05:36] Marcus: can you give a concrete p95 example for 13B streaming, like 1k tokens prompt, 6k tokens stream at 60 tok/sec?
[05:44] Lina: rough calc — streaming throughput depends more on token emit rate, the runtime can sustain ~60-100 tok/sec on optimized paths for a 13B quantized in host decks, p95 per-chunk depends on batching; we'd propose a benchmark where we simulate 200 concurrent streams at 60 t/s for 10 minutes.

[08:00] Ethan: question about KV cache and prefix caching — does Redwood do automatic prefix cache to avoid redoing context? we have a lot of repeated preambles.
[08:08] Lina: yes we have both prefix caching and KV cache reuse across requests on the same session, that reduces per-token compute. But cache locality matters — dedicated gives more durable caches, hosted uses ephemeral instances but we do cross-instance cache invalidation strategies and smart routing to increase cache hits.
[08:27] Marcus: how often do cache misses happen on hosted under burst?
[08:31] Lina: depends, but we see hit rates drop during large bursts; we compensate with routing policy to favor instances with warm cache and by using a shared prefix store for common prompts. we'll need to test with your exact prompt set.

[11:00] Olivia: security — we need KMS/HSM integration and audit logs, SOC2 is baseline, can you confirm private deployment options?
[11:09] Evan: yes, Redwood private includes customer-managed KMS, private control plane, and audit log exports. we also support dedicated with VPC peering and bring-your-own-key for encryption at rest.
[11:21] Olivia: and SSO/SAML integration for role-based access?
[11:24] Lina: yes we support SSO, RBAC, and per-model access controls; note some enterprise features are part of private or higher enterprise tiers.

[14:00] Marcus: timeline — we want a production pilot by Q4, are there fast paths?
[14:07] Evan: typically a pilot on hosted is fastest — get 1-2 endpoints up in days, then scale to dedicated/reserved for predictability. For private it's a bit longer — network setup and compliance checks add 4-8 weeks.
[14:21] Priya: for our bench plan we want to measure p95 for small completions and streaming sustained token/sec across models and quantization levels.
[14:29] Lina: we'll propose a benchmark matrix: model configs (13B q4, 13B fp16, 70B q4m), payload sizes (short: <300 tokens, mid: 1k prompt + 1k stream, long: 1k prompt + 6k stream), concurrency levels (10/50/150/200), measure p95 first-token latency, median throughput, and token/sec sustained.
[14:50] Marcus: that matrix sounds good. we also want to include fallback behaviors — e.g., if hosted is saturated, can requests be downgraded to a smaller model gracefully?
[14:58] Lina: yes, routing policies support version downgrade fallback or region fallback; you can set latency thresholds that trigger a cheaper model variant. we can demo how that affects quality with A/B.

[18:30] Priya: cost question — what's the unit economics for streaming tokens on hosted vs dedicated?
[18:36] Evan: hosted is pay-as-you-go; dedicated gives a reserved instance price which amortizes better at scale. we'll provide a cost model spreadsheet; quick rule: if sustained throughput exceeds X tokens/sec per month, dedicated typically becomes 25-40% cheaper depending on model and utilization.
[18:50] Marcus: what about preemptible GPUs? we need reliability, preemptibles might be cheaper but could harm p95 SLA.
[18:58] Lina: we don't recommend preemptibles for p95-sensitive streaming. Dedicated reserved capacity is for predictable latency. For hosted we mix instance types and fallbacks to preserve SLAs.

[22:00] Olivia: for the SOC2 docs, can you provide evidence of audit logs retention period and key rotation?
[22:08] Evan: yes we'll share our security pack; for private we can align to customer retention and rotation schedules.

[25:00] Marcus: regarding burst handling — do you have a recommended queuing strategy if we oversubscribe? we'd rather degrade gracefully than error.
[25:08] Lina: we provide graceful throttling, queueing with estimated wait times, and automatic fallback to smaller models or cached summaries. for streaming specifically we can return partial summaries if full stream can't be sustained.
[25:28] Ethan: how transparent is the latency breakdown? we want token-level tracing.
[25:33] Lina: Console provides token-level cost/latency breakdown, per-route dashboards, and traces. we can instrument a request to show kv cache hit/miss and per-token emit times.

[30:00] Marcus: ok hypotheticals — if we run a benchmark and p95 is 650ms for short responses on hosted, what are the next levers?
[30:08] Lina: levers: switch to quantized kernel, enable prefix cache aggressively, tune batching window, route to dedicated reserved nodes, or lower model size. each has tradeoffs on quality. we can run a tuning pass and present a prioritized plan.
[30:30] Marcus: can you give an estimate for time-to-run a tuning pass?
[30:33] Lina: initial benchmark + tuning takes ~2 weeks assuming test infra is provisioned, bench agents provided, and we can run in your environment or ours.

[33:00] Priya: integration specifics — do you provide an SDK for streaming and session management?
[33:06] Evan: yes SDKs for node/python, streaming APIs with reconnect semantics, session tokens and KV attach. samples for rehydrating cache and replaying tokens.

[36:00] Olivia: data residency — we store logs for 30 days by default, can we extend?
[36:06] Lina: yes tunable retention on enterprise tiers and private. for hosted we have configurable retention windows and export hooks.

[39:00] Marcus: any gotchas for quantized 13B streaming that we should know?
[39:06] Lina: quantization can slightly increase token latency jitter; however optimized kernels and lower precision enable higher tok/sec. we'll include recommended quant profiles per model and workload in the bench plan.

[41:30] Evan: ok let's recap next steps — Lina will draft benchmark plan and runbook; I'll send pricing and hosted vs dedicated cost model; Olivia will share compliance checklist; we schedule a 60-minute benchmarking session week of 7/20.
[41:50] Marcus: that works. also please include example metrics we'd expect from the run so we can baseline.
[41:56] Lina: yes, we'll provide example p95 reports and token-level traces.

[44:00] Olivia: last Q — for private deployment networking, do you support air-gapped installs?
[44:06] Evan: yes we have an on-prem package for air-gapped environments, it has a longer lead time for provisioning and validation.

[45:10] Marcus: thanks everyone, appreciate the clarity. we'll review the bench plan and sync on dates.
[45:18] Evan: thanks all, we'll follow up with materials by EOD Friday.

[46:00] Meeting end.
